Question B-003-016-003.

Why the correct answer is right: A storage battery is a rechargeable battery: electrical energy can be put back into it by a suitable charger after discharge.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "low leakage battery": Low leakage describes a cell that loses charge slowly or is less prone to electrolyte leakage; it does not mean the cell can be repeatedly recharged.
- sourceIndex 2: "memory battery": Memory battery is not the general class name for a rechargeable station battery; it can also be confused with small backup cells used to preserve settings.
- sourceIndex 3: "primary battery": A primary battery is intended for single discharge and replacement, so it is the opposite of the rechargeable battery being described.
